commits.message:
[NVIDIA] Fold warpid to 0 for single-warp partitions in warp specialize to llvm conversion (#12498)

If a warp specialization partition is assigned only 1 warp, the relative
warp id must be zero. Folding this to zero allow LLVM to remove a
conditional branch on the warp id in the MMAv5 lowering that guarantees
only (one thread elected from) one warp issues a `tcgen05.mma`.

The `nvgpu_to_llvm` pass has supported this fold since #6823, but after
the warp specialization conversion pass was moved before `nvgpu_to_llvm`
in #9535, the fold no longer covers the common scenario, as the
partition is already lowered so the `lookupNumWarps` helper sees the
number of warps of the module instead of the partition.

Fix: folds `ttg.warp_id` to zero during warp specialization conversion,
while the partition's warp count is still available.

This can be reproduced from
[08-warp-specialization.py](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/main/python/tutorials/gluon/08-warp-specialization.py),
compiled for sm100:

    ...
    for _ in range(scheduler.get_num_tiles()):
        # Acquire the accumulator for the entire inner loop.
        ...
        for k in range(0, K, BLOCK_K):
            # Acquire operands, issue MMA, and complete asynchronously.
            mbarrier.wait(load_ready_bars.index(load_state.index), load_state.phase)
            tcgen05_mma(p.a_bufs.index(load_state.index), p.b_bufs.index(load_state.index), acc_buf, use_acc=use_acc)
            tcgen05_commit(load_empty_bars.index(load_state.index))
            load_state = load_state.next()
            use_acc = True
     ...

def matmul_warp_specialized_kernel(a_desc, b_desc, c_desc, SchedulerImpl: gl.constexpr, num_buffers: gl.constexpr,
                                   SUBTILE_FACTOR: gl.constexpr, num_warps: gl.constexpr):

commits.message:
[AMD] Add MIR dump/swap to AMD CodeGen LLVM (#12122)

Second of three changes moving the MIR dump/swap stage (`TRITON_DUMP_MIR`,
`TRITON_SWAP_MIR`) from Triton's core LLVM onto the AMD code generator's
LLVM, so dumped and rescheduled MIR comes from the same compiler as the
shipped code. Builds on #12123. Nothing calls the new code yet, so this is a
no-op at runtime.

Adds two entry points to `libtriton_amd_codegen.so`:

- `triton_amdgpu_translate_to_mir`: LLVM IR to MIR text plus scheduling DAG.
- `triton_amdgpu_translate_mir_to_asm`: MIR text to AMDGCN assembly or object.

They share `triton_amdgpu_compile`'s module prologue, return buffers instead
of touching the filesystem, and report errors through `fail()` instead of
`report_fatal_error`.

Other changes:

- `codegenABIVersion` goes to 2 for two new trailing `CodegenOptions` fields.
- `DAGBuilder.{h,cpp}` move into `backend/codegen/`. The core library compiles
  the same file until the follow-up drops its MIR path. Its sinks
  become `thread_local`, so concurrent dumps don't clobber each other.
- All entry points drain `-time-passes` and share a `publish()` helper.

[CD] Build free-threaded 3.14t and 3.15t wheels (#12502)

## What
Build `cp314t` and `cp315t` wheels in `wheels.yml`, next to the existing
`cp311` version-specific wheel. They go through the same `cibuildwheel`
invocation, with the regular (non-abi3) environment.

## Why
#10958 made the Python 3.12+ wheel an abi3 wheel (`cp312-abi3`). abi3
wheels cannot be used on free-threaded interpreters: pip's tag logic
rejects `cp312-abi3` on 3.14t and 3.15t, and PEP 803 lists `cp314-abi3`
/ `cp315-abi3` as incompatible with free-threaded builds. So
free-threaded users currently get no triton wheel from this workflow,
and downstream (PyTorch) has to build them separately.

3.13t stays out (#10547): manylinux dropped it. The current manylinux
README lists 3.14t and 3.15t.

## Checks
- `cibuildwheel` 4.3.4 lists `cp314t-manylinux_{x86_64,aarch64}` and
`cp315t-manylinux_{x86_64,aarch64}` with the `CIBW_BUILD` / `CIBW_SKIP`
values from this workflow, no `--enable` needed.
- The abi3 build keeps its own `CIBW_ENVIRONMENT` with
`TRITON_STABLE_ABI=ON`; the free-threaded builds don't set it.
- Not built end to end yet. Run time: the two existing builds take about
50-55 min per job, so four builds should stay well under the 180 min
timeout; the PR run of this workflow will show the real number.

## Stale manylinux image on the self-hosted runner
The first run of this PR failed on the self-hosted x86_64 runner: it
reused a cached `quay.io/pypa/manylinux_2_28_x86_64:latest` that
predates CPython 3.15 (its interpreter list stops at cp314 and still has
cp313t, which upstream manylinux dropped in May), so
`manylinux-interpreters ensure cp315-cp315t` failed. The workflow now
`docker pull`s the image before building and prunes the untagged one it
leaves behind. The GitHub-hosted aarch64 runner starts fresh and is
unaffected.

## Note
`release/3.9.x` has its own copy of `wheels.yml`; this PR does not
change it.

commits.message:
[AMD][Gluon] Add buffer.atomic_load and buffer.atomic_store (#12493)

Add `amdg.buffer_atomic_load` / `amdg.buffer_atomic_store`, the buffer
counterparts of `tt.atomic_load` / `tt.atomic_store`, and expose them as
`cdna{3,4}.buffer.atomic_load` / `atomic_store`. They take a buffer
descriptor (or pointer), offsets, an optional mask and `soffset`, and
the usual `sem` (acquire/relaxed for loads, release/relaxed for stores)
and `scope`.

Loads lower to `llvm.amdgcn.raw.ptr.atomic.buffer.load`, which LLVM
never removes or hoists, so a relaxed atomic load can poll a flag in a
loop. LLVM has no atomic buffer store intrinsic, so stores lower to a
plain buffer store, as LLVM's own lowering of atomic stores through
buffer pointers does. Both set the scope's coherence bits (SC0/SC1) on
the access and get the same program-level ordering as the `tt` atomics:
CTA barriers around the op and an acquire or release fence at the scope.
As with `tt.atomic_load`, one thread loads each element and broadcasts
it to the element's other copies.

commits.comment: 重写 AMD 软件路径 fp8e4nv→fp16 上转：把逐元素 i16 位移+加常量+8 项 denorm LUT 的实现换成两两打包进 i32、以 vector<2xf16> 乘 2^(15-7) 一步完成 rebias 与次正规数规范化（与 fp8→bf16 路径一致），NaN 仍逐元素检查；前提是 fp16 denorm 不被 flush（当前后端只设置 denormal-fp-math-f32，成立）。使 RDNA3 上该转换从“不支持”变为支持，并纳入测试覆盖（新增 all-encodings 测试、启用 RDNA3 上 fp8e4nv 上转）。性能上对部分 GEMM 有约 3x 提升。风险点：隐含依赖 LLVM 不对 fp16 denorm 做 flush，若将来设置变化会静默产生错误结果；已用注释说明。

commits.message:
[AMD] Speed up SW fp8e4nv -> fp16 upcast with packed fmul (#12492)

The software fp8e4nv -> fp16 path (used on RDNA3 and CDNA2/3) rebiased
the exponent with an integer add and then fixed up subnormals with an
8-entry select LUT per element. Instead, multiply by 2^(15-7) in fp16,
which rebiases the exponent and normalizes subnormals in one step, as
the fp8 -> bf16 path already does. Values are converted in pairs packed
into an i32, so masking and sign handling use 32-bit ops and the rebias
is a single packed multiply. NaN is still checked per element.

This requires fp16 denormals to be preserved, which holds today since
the backend only sets `denormal-fp-math-f32`.

This can improve runtime 3x for some GEMM kernels on RDNA3.

Signed-off-by: Pengzhan Zhao <borontion@gmail.com>

commits.comment: 本次最大改动：为 Blackwell MMAv5 落地 two-CTA 模式（PTX 13+ 要求同一 kernel 内 tcgen 指令 CTA 模式一致，故在 AccelerateMatmul 中以 canUseTwoCTAsInModule 一次性决定整个 module 是否启用）。实现要点：(1) 仅对 descriptor/TMA 加载的 A、B 启用，通过 getTwoCTADescriptorLoad/inferTwoCTAOperandLayouts 沿 reshape/transpose/split 等 view 链传播 RHS 沿 N 分裂的 CGA layout；B 的 CGA 分裂把 block 维 basis 映射为 [[0,1],[0,0],[0,2]] 形式；对 4/8 CTA 要求相邻 CTA 配对，并列形式给出多种不支持回退条件（N<16、fp8 时 N<32、M>128、N>256、标量 dot_scaled 等）。(2) createTMABarrierAndWait 对“仅被 MMA/等待消费”的 MMA-only 加载组改用 pair-shared barrier（createBarrierAlloc 新增 twoCTAs 参数，createScalarAlloc 中构造配对 CGA layout 并将 memdesc 形状改为 {numBuffers, numCTAs/2}），否则在 wait 之后插入 ttng.cluster_barrier。(3) createBarrierAndWaitOps 在 two_ctas 时把完成 barrier 环扩到 max(numStages, schedule.getNumStages())，避免两槽复用导致的 peer 死锁。(4) 新增 protectTwoCTAAccumulatorReuse：在 TMEM 读取后加 pair-shared arrive、在两 CTA 复用累加器前 wait，支持单/多 reader、嵌套 scf.if、条件读取（通过额外 iter_args 传 ring index/phase），并将不支持的嵌套循环读取保持原样（保守不插入）。(5) AssignLatencies/AutomaticWarpSpecialization 在 two-CTA 时禁用自动 warp specialization；TMALowering 非流水 TMA 在 two-CTA module 中插入 cluster_barrier；HoistMBarrierLifecycle 移除 two-CTA 的 assert 并用 DominanceInfo 安全地 hoist 初始 phase（避免把被外层条件共用的常量 sink 进 then 区）。改动了 PipeliningUtility.h 的 createScalarAlloc/createBarrierAlloc 签名（新增默认参数，向后兼容）。测试覆盖 accelerate-matmul、pipeline-lower-loop、automatic-warp-specialization、hoist-mbarrier-lifecycle、tma_lowering 的 lit 用例以及 test_matmul.py 的 two-CTA 端到端与教程。风险较高：涉及同步协议、TMEM 复用与 pipeline 调度多处语义，若某些视图链或 reader 形态未覆盖则可能死锁或读脏数据；同时对带默认参数的头文件签名变更虽向后兼容，但下游若按旧签名重载需注意。

ascend_impact.functionality: 无影响。改动全部位于 NVIDIA 专属路径：TritonGPU 的 AccelerateMatmul/Pipeliner/warp-specialization（其中 two-CTA 分支由 ttng.two-ctas 属性与 NvidiaMmaEncoding 门控，Ascend 不产生这些条件）、TritonNvidiaGPU 方言 pass，以及教程。PipeliningUtility.h 中 createScalarAlloc/createBarrierAlloc 新增的 twoCTAs 为默认参数，不改变 Ascend 的调用方式。

commits.comment: 修复 AMD WMMA 操作数在 kWidth 跨多条指令时的寄存器定位错误。原实现用 K 坐标对 dot layout 的伪逆取 startReg 再连续读 kBase 个寄存器，当 16x16x16（kBase=8）、kWidth=16 时两条指令都解析到寄存器 0，导致 8-15 从未被读取、结果静默错误。修复为：getInstrsPerKChunk 计算每个 kWidth chunk 覆盖的指令数（kWidth / kPerSubtile），kElemIdx 定位到 chunk 起点，startReg 加上 (kIdx % instrsPerChunk) * kPerSubtile 的 chunk 内偏移；padding 循环改用 subTileStride = kPerSubtile * instrsPerChunk（保证 subtile 跨越整块 chunk）。同时在 TritonGPU InferLayoutInterface 中为 WMMA v2+ 增加校验：当 kWidth*2 > instrShape[2] 且 K < kWidth*2 时报错 'WMMA dot operand kWidth = X requires K >= Y'，避免 chunk 被广播到不同 K 的 lane 而产生错误。附带 wmma2 kWidth=16 与 wmma3 f32 kWidth=8 的 lowering lit 用例、verifier 负例以及 CDNA4 上 wide kWidth 的端到端 GEMM 测试。双操作数的 K 置换一致，求和不变，故正确性修复不影响数值语义（除原错误场景）。

commits.message:
[AMD] Fix WMMA operands whose kWidth spans several instructions (#12477)

A WMMA v2 dot operand with kWidth = 16 and a 16x16x16 instruction (kBase
= 8) is accepted by the verifier and gives a valid layout: each lane
holds 16 contiguous K elements, so one kWidth chunk covers two
instructions. The lowering, however, located each instruction's
registers by pseudo-inverting its first K coordinate and reading kBase
consecutive registers from there. Both instructions of a chunk resolved
to register 0, so registers 8-15 were never read and the dot silently
produced wrong results (max abs error ~30 for a 64x64x64 f16 GEMM on
gfx1201).

Locate the chunk start instead and offset each instruction to its part
of the chunk. The resulting K permutation is the same for A and B, so
the sum over K is unchanged. Subtiles along the non-K dimension are then
a whole chunk apart.

A chunk spanning several instructions is only valid when the dot's K
covers it; otherwise the layout broadcasts its elements to lanes the
instructions read as different K. Reject that case in the dot verifier.
